mainTopic: Vows of מנחות in a מחבת, a מרחשת and an oven, and the sources for each view
overview: The משנה rules that if someone vows a מנחה made in a מחבת, he may not bring it in a מרחשת, and the reverse is also true. רבי יוסי הגלילי says the difference is that a מרחשת has a cover. רבי חנינא בן גמליאל says a מרחשת is deep and a מחבת is flat. The גמרא shows that wordplay on the names cannot prove רבי יוסי הגלילי's view, so it must be a tradition. רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's view comes from the פסוק: 'in' the מרחשת and 'on' the מחבת. A ברייתא then brings בית שמאי, who are unsure whether these names refer to vessels or to how the מנחה is made. בית הלל prove they are names of vessels. A second משנה discusses a vow of a מנחה baked 'in an oven' and whether loaves and wafers may be mixed. The גמרא brings the sources for each view, and רבא answers a challenge to רבי שמעון. The amud ends as רבי שמעון begins his reply to רבי יהודה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A vow for one pan cannot be paid with the other
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a מנחה vowed in a מחבת cannot be brought in a מרחשת, and the reverse is also true.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNAH: If someone says, 'I take upon myself to bring a meal offering made in a מחבת,' he may not bring one made in a מרחשת. If he said 'in a מרחשת,' he may not bring one made in a מחבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets the basic rule. Whatever pan you named in your vow is the pan you must use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two pans count as different kinds of מנחה. Naming one in a vow makes it binding, so switching to the other does not fulfill the vow. This raises an obvious question: what actually makes the two pans different?

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה being studied
'It is upon me': the wording of a vow to bring an offering
A pan used to cook one type of מנחה
A different pan used to cook another type of מנחה

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who says: "It is upon me in a machavat"
phrases.notes: He means he vows to bring a meal offering cooked in that pan.

phrases.english: may not bring it in a marcheshet;
if he said "in a marcheshet," he may not bring it in a machavat.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow that names one pan must be fulfilled with that pan. The other pan does not count.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: the difference is a cover
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks how the two pans differ. רבי יוסי הגלילי answers that a מרחשת has a cover and a מחבת does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between a מחבת and a מרחשת? A מרחשת has a cover, and a מחבת has no cover. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks what separates the two pans and gives the first answer, from רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי הגלילי, the difference he names is whether the pan has a lid, not its depth.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is the difference between...'
A cover or lid

phrases.english: What is the difference between a machavat and a marcheshet?
A marcheshet has a cover,
a machavat has no cover;
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the two pans whose difference the rule in step 1 depends on
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מרחשת has a cover. A מחבת has no cover.

steps.title: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל: deep versus flat
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל says a מרחשת is deep and makes soft food, while a מחבת is flat and makes hard food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל says: A מרחשת is deep, and what is made in it moves about (and is soft). A מחבת is flat, and what is made in it is hard.
steps.whatsHappening: A second view explains the difference by the depth of the pan and the texture of the food it produces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view looks at the pan's shape and how the food comes out, not at whether it has a lid. Food in the deep pan moves around and stays soft. Food in the flat pan comes out hard.

keyTerms.meaning: Deep
Moving about, bubbling
Flat, shallow
Hard

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two views. רבי יוסי הגלילי talks about a lid. רבי חנינא בן גמליאל talks about deep versus flat.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel says:
A marcheshet is deep
and what is made in it moves about (soft);
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't. It means the food comes out soft.

phrases.english: a machavat is flat, and what is made in it is hard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different definition of the two pans from the one in step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מרחשת is deep and makes soft food. A מחבת is flat and makes hard food.

steps.title: What is the source for רבי יוסי הגלילי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי יוסי הגלילי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: What is the reason of רבי יוסי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking where רבי יוסי הגלילי got the idea of a covered pan versus an uncovered one. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah never says that one pan has a lid. So the גמרא wants to know what source or reasoning lies behind this view.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows the משנה
'What is the reason?'

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or reasoning for saying that a מרחשת has a cover and a מחבת does not

steps.title: A suggested source from the meaning of the names
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that מרחשת is linked to the hidden stirrings of the heart, and מחבת to the open sins of the mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say: מרחשת is called that because it comes for the stirrings of the heart, as it is written, 'My heart stirs with a good matter.' And מחבת is called that because it comes for the openings of the mouth, as people say, 'He is barking away.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer. It reads hidden meanings into the names of the two pans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name מרחשת is linked to the heart, which is hidden, so it would fit a covered pan. The name מחבת is linked to the mouth, which speaks out in the open, so it would fit an uncovered pan. The word אילימא ('if you say') signals that this suggestion is about to be knocked down.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you say': introduces a suggestion that will probably be rejected
The stirrings or musings of the heart
The openings of the mouth, meaning things done with speech
'As people say': a common saying

phrases.english: If you say: marcheshet,
because it comes for the stirrings of the heart,
as it is written: "My heart stirs with a good matter,"
and machavat, because it comes for the openings of the mouth,
as people say: "He is barking away."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the question in step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The names of the pans hint at hidden thoughts of the heart (covered pan) versus open speech of the mouth (uncovered pan).

steps.title: The wordplay works just as well in reverse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the same kind of wordplay can link מחבת to the heart and מרחשת to the mouth, so the suggestion proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the opposite: מחבת comes for the hidden things of the heart, as it is written, 'Why did you hide yourself to flee?' And מרחשת comes for the movements of [the mouth], as people say, 'His lips were moving.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggested source by showing that the opposite reading is just as easy to make.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מחבת sounds like נחבא, 'hidden', which would make it the covered pan. מרחשת can describe lips moving, which would make it the uncovered pan. Since the wordplay can go either way, it cannot prove which pan has the cover.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say the reverse': the same logic could give the opposite result
You hid yourself
His lips

phrases.english: Say the opposite:
machavat, because it comes for the hidden things of the heart,
as it is written: "Why did you hide yourself to flee?"
marcheshet, because it comes for the movements of [the mouth],
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: as people say: "His lips were moving."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source suggested in step 5
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole attempt to derive רבי יוסי הגלילי's view from the names of the pans
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The wordplay can be reversed just as easily, so it cannot decide which pan has the cover.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי's view is a received tradition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי יוסי הגלילי knew the difference from a tradition, not from wordplay.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he learned it as a received tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: Since no source from the names works, the גמרא says the definition was simply handed down as a tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in step 4 is not answered with a פסוק. Instead, the גמרא says the source is a tradition passed down from teacher to student. That closes this part of the discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They learned it as a tradition': a teaching handed down rather than derived from a פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי הגלילי's lid-or-no-lid definition comes from a tradition. Wordplay on the names fails because it works both ways.
steps.confusionAlert: Here גמרא does not mean the Talmud. It means a teaching that was handed down as a tradition.

phrases.english: Rather, they learned it as a received tradition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the rejection in step 6, gives the final answer to the question in step 4
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוסי הגלילי's definition is a received tradition, not something derived from the names of the pans.

steps.title: A פסוק source for רבי חנינא בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's view comes from the פסוק: 'in' the מרחשת but 'on' the מחבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל says, and so on. A מרחשת is deep, as it is written, 'And all that is made in the מרחשת.' A מחבת is flat, as it is written, 'And on the מחבת.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second view from the משנה and finds its source in the wording of a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says food is made 'in' the מרחשת, so it must be a deep pan with room inside. It says food is made 'on' the מחבת, so it must be a flat pan. This view has a clear source in the text, unlike רבי יוסי הגלילי's view, which rests on tradition.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Etc.': short for the rest of the quote
'In the מרחשת': the word 'in' points to a deep pan
'And on the מחבת': the word 'on' points to a flat pan

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל learns his view from the פסוק: 'in' the מרחשת means it is deep, and 'on' the מחבת means it is flat.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel says, etc.
A marcheshet is deep,
as it is written: "And all that is made in the marcheshet,"
a machavat is flat,
as it is written: "And on the machavat."
phrases.notes: Same פסוק. The switch from 'in' to 'on' is the whole proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר כּוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from רבי יוסי הגלילי's view to find the source for the second view in the משנה
steps.raayaObject: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's view that a מרחשת is deep and a מחבת is flat
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 7:9: 'in' the מרחשת versus 'on' the מחבת

steps.title: בית שמאי: A vow of "a מרחשת" must wait until אליהו comes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that according to בית שמאי, someone who vows "הרי עלי מרחשת" cannot fulfill the vow yet. It must be set aside until אליהו comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: בית שמאי say: If someone says "I take upon myself a מרחשת," it should be set aside until אליהו comes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a person who vowed "a מרחשת" without making clear exactly what he meant. בית שמאי say nothing can be done until אליהו comes and clears it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person did not say "a מנחה made in a מרחשת." He only said "a מרחשת." בית שמאי treat his meaning as unclear, so the matter stays on hold. The next step explains what they are unsure about.

keyTerms.meaning: "I take upon myself": the standard wording for a vow to bring something to the מקדש
A deep pan used for one type of מנחה; it can also be the name of that מנחה
Until אליהו comes: the matter stays unresolved until he clarifies it

phrases.english: The Sages taught: Beit Shammai say:
One who says: "It is upon me to bring a marcheshet"
it should be set aside until Eliyahu comes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about the meaning of the word מרחשת in a vow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, a vow of "a מרחשת" stays unresolved until אליהו comes.

steps.title: Why בית שמאי are unsure: named for the vessel, or for how it is made?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that בית שמאי do not know whether the names מרחשת and מחבת come from the vessels or from the way each מנחה is prepared.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are unsure whether these offerings are named for the vessel or named for the way they are made.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind בית שמאי's ruling. They have a real doubt about where the name comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If מרחשת is the name of a vessel, the person may have vowed to donate the vessel itself. If the name describes how the מנחה is made, he vowed to bring that kind of מנחה. Since בית שמאי cannot decide which is right, they leave the vow on hold.

keyTerms.meaning: They are unsure; it is a doubt for them
Named because of the vessel
How they are made; the way they are prepared

phrases.english: They are uncertain,
whether they are called by these names because of the vessel,
or because of the way they are made.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind בית שמאי's ruling in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why would בית שמאי leave the vow unresolved?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They are unsure whether the name refers to the vessel or to the way the מנחה is made.

steps.title: בית הלל: There was a vessel in the מקדש called מרחשת
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל say there is no doubt. There was a real vessel in the מקדש named מרחשת. It looked like a deep כלבוס, and dough placed inside took on the shape of round fruits.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל say: There was a vessel in the מקדש, and its name was מרחשת. It looked like a kind of deep כלבוס. When dough was placed inside it, the dough looked like a kind of apple of the ברתים tree and like a kind of Greek acorn.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל answer בית שמאי's doubt by saying מרחשת was the actual name of a vessel in the מקדש. They describe what it looked like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By showing that a real vessel carried this name, בית הלל settle the doubt in favor of "named for the vessel." The description explains the shape: dough pressed into the pan's dents came out looking like rounded fruits.

keyTerms.meaning: The בית המקדש, the Temple
A kind of vessel with dents or hollows in it
Dough
Greek acorns: round nuts that the shaped dough looked like

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say:
There was a vessel in the Temple,
and its name was "marcheshet,"
and it looked like a kind of deep kelabus,
and when dough is placed inside it,
it looks like a kind of apple of the beratim trees
phrases.notes: Here "it" is the dough, pressed into the pan's shape, not the pan itself.

phrases.english: and like a kind of Greek acorn.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: כְּלִי הָיָה בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives בית הלל's side, which rejects בית שמאי's doubt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מרחשת is the name of a real vessel that was in the מקדש.

steps.title: Proof from "in the מרחשת and on the מחבת": the names come from the vessels
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says a מנחה is made "in" the מרחשת and "on" the מחבת. This shows the names come from the vessels, not from the way the מנחה is made.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the פסוק says: "And all that is made in the מרחשת and on the מחבת." So clearly they are named for the vessels, and not for the way they are made.
steps.whatsHappening: A פסוק is brought to support בית הלל. The words "in" and "on" describe where the dough sits in a vessel, so these names must belong to the vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You put something "in" or "on" a physical object, not "in" a cooking method. Since the פסוק uses these words, מרחשת and מחבת are vessels. This settles the doubt of step 10 in favor of "named for the vessel."

keyTerms.meaning: "And it says": introduces a פסוק as support
A flat pan used for another type of מנחה
"Evidently" or "so we see": introduces the conclusion drawn from a proof

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי are unsure whether מרחשת is a vessel's name or a way of making the מנחה, so they leave the vow on hold. בית הלל prove from "in the מרחשת" and "on the מחבת" that these are names of vessels.
steps.confusionAlert: Step 8 used this same פסוק to show the difference between the two pans. Here the same words prove something else: that both names belong to vessels at all.

phrases.english: And it says:
"And all that is made in the marcheshet and on the machavat,"
evidently they are called by these names because of the vessels,
and not because of the way they are made.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹמֵר: וְכׇל נַעֲשָׂה בַמַּרְחֶשֶׁת וְעַל מַחֲבַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a פסוק to support בית הלל's claim in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: בית הלל's claim that the names מרחשת and מחבת come from the vessels
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 7:9: "in the מרחשת and on the מחבת"

steps.title: Vowing a מנחה baked in an oven
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that someone who vows a מנחה baked 'in an oven' may not bake it on a כופח, roof tiles, or in Arab baking pits. רבי יהודה allows a כופח.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says, 'I take upon myself a מנחה baked in an oven,' he may not bring one baked on a small stove, on roof tiles, or in the baking pits of the Arabs. רבי יהודה says: if he wants, he may bring one baked on a small stove.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It defines what counts as an 'oven' for someone who vowed a מנחה baked in a תנור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says only a real תנור counts. A small stove, roof tiles, and ground pits are all excluded. רבי יהודה disagrees only about the כופח and treats it as a kind of oven.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (short form: מַתְנִי׳)
'It is upon me': the wording of a נדר to bring a קרבן
An oven
A small stove or oven
Roof tiles
Baking pits used by Arabs

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
[If one says:] It is upon me [to bring a meal offering baked] in an oven,
he may not bring one baked on a small stove,
nor one baked on roof tiles,
and [not] one baked in the baking pits of the Arabs.
phrases.notes: The 'not' carries over from the lines before, so this one is left out too.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If he wishes, he may bring one baked on a small stove.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of מרחשת and מחבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow of a מנחה baked in an oven excludes a כופח, roof tiles, and Arab pits. רבי יהודה allows a כופח.

steps.title: Mixing loaves and wafers in a baked מנחה
steps.stepSummary: Someone who vows a מנחת מאפה may not bring half חלות and half רקיקין. רבי שמעון allows it because it is one קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says, 'I take upon myself a baked מנחה,' he may not bring half as loaves and half as wafers. רבי שמעון permits it, because it is one offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case about a baked מנחה. The question is whether one offering can be split between the two allowed forms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מנחת מאפה can be made as thick loaves or as thin wafers. The תנא קמא requires the whole offering to be one form. רבי שמעון says both forms belong to one single קרבן, so mixing them is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: A מנחה baked in an oven
Thick loaves
Thin wafers
One single offering

phrases.english: [If one says:] It is upon me [to bring] a baked meal offering,
he may not bring half as loaves
and half as wafers;
Rabbi Shimon permits it,
because it is one offering.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has two arguments. One is about which ovens count (רבי יהודה allows a כופח). The other is about mixing חלות and רקיקין (רבי שמעון allows it).
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case in the same משנה about a baked מנחה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vowed מנחת מאפה may not be split half חלות and half רקיקין. רבי שמעון permits it.

steps.title: The פסוק source for excluding other baking surfaces
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'מאפה תנור' as limiting the מנחה to a real oven. This excludes a כופח, roof tiles, and Arab pits, matching the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'Baked in an oven.' This means not baked on a small stove, not on roof tiles, and not in the baking pits of the Arabs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion. It brings a ברייתא showing where the תנא קמא of the משנה gets his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק specifically says 'תנור'. So anything that is not a true oven is left out. This is the source for the first opinion in step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה (short form: גְּמָ׳)
'Baked in an oven': the wording of the פסוק
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Rabbis taught:
"Baked in an oven"
and not baked on a small stove,
and not baked on roof tiles,
and not baked in the baking pits of the Arabs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק source for the תנא קמא of the first case in the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The תנא קמא's rule that only a real oven counts
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words 'מאפה תנור' in ויקרא ב:ד

steps.title: רבי יהודה includes the כופח from the double 'oven'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה notes that 'תנור' appears twice in the תורה. He uses the repetition to make a כופח valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: 'Oven' and 'oven' are written two times, to make a מנחה baked on a small stove valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives רבי יהודה's source for his opinion in the משנה that a כופח is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'תנור' appears in two פסוקים. רבי יהודה reads the extra mention as widening the law, not narrowing it. So the כופח also counts as an oven.

keyTerms.meaning: Two times: the word is repeated
To make valid or fit

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
"Oven," "oven": two times,
to render valid one baked on a small stove.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: תַּנּוּר תַּנּוּר שְׁנֵי פְּעָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's reading and gives the source for רבי יהודה's opinion in the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's ruling that a כופח is valid
steps.raayaSupportSource: The repetition of 'תנור' in two פסוקים

steps.title: רבי שמעון uses the two mentions for two laws
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון uses the two mentions of 'תנור' for two separate laws. The מנחה must be baked in an oven, and the oven is what makes it holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: 'Oven' and 'oven' are written two times. One teaches that their baking must be in an oven. The other teaches that their becoming holy happens in the oven.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives a different use for the double word 'תנור'. He does not use it to include a כופח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה used the second 'תנור' to widen the law. רבי שמעון says the second mention has its own job. It teaches that the oven itself makes these מנחות holy, so he does not use it to include a כופח. The next steps challenge this reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Their baking
Their becoming holy (consecration)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
"Oven," "oven": two times,
one, that their baking should be in an oven,
and one, that their consecration should be in the oven.
phrases.notes: He means the oven itself makes the מנחה holy, instead of a holy service vessel doing it.

steps.confusionAlert: This רבי שמעון is not giving the source for his own opinion in the משנה about mixing חלות and רקיקין. Here he is explaining the two mentions of 'תנור'.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a classic גמרא pattern. When a repeated word is needed for a different law, it can no longer be used to widen the rule. Here רבי שמעון uses the second 'תנור' for its own law rather than to include a כופח.
steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: תַּנּוּר תַּנּוּר שְׁנֵי פְּעָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different use for the same double word that רבי יהודה used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One 'תנור' requires baking in an oven. The other teaches that מנחות of this kind become holy in the oven.

steps.title: Does רבי שמעון really hold the oven makes the מנחה holy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון's view that the oven makes the מנחה holy. It cites a משנה where he says the שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים are valid even when prepared outside the עזרה, in בית פאגי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי שמעון really think this way? But we learned in a משנה that רבי שמעון says: you should always get used to saying that the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים are valid if made in the עזרה, and also valid if made in בית פאגי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks what רבי שמעון said in step 17, that the oven is what makes the מנחה holy. It brings a contradiction from another משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the oven made bread holy, then baking it outside the holy area should make it פסול, because holy things become invalid when taken out. But רבי שמעון says bread baked in בית פאגי, outside the walls, is still valid. That suggests the oven does not make the bread holy.

keyTerms.meaning: line of reasoning, view
the two loaves brought on שבועות
the showbread placed on the שולחן
the Temple courtyard
a place outside the walls of the Temple Mount

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about where bread is usually baked. It is about whether the bread is already holy while it is in the oven. If it were, baking it outside would make it פסול.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הַאי סְבָרָא?
phrases.english: And does Rabbi Shimon hold this reasoning?
But didn't we learn: Rabbi Shimon says:
One should always be accustomed to say
the two loaves and the showbread
are valid in the courtyard,
and are valid in Beit Pagei.
phrases.notes: Beit Pagei is outside the holy area. So going outside does not ruin this bread, which means it was not holy yet.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הַאי סְבָרָא? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second law רבי שמעון derived in step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's claim that the oven makes the מנחה holy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the oven made the bread holy, bread baked outside the holy area would be פסול. Yet רבי שמעון says bread made in בית פאגי is valid.

steps.title: רבא: the oven requirement is about how the owner dedicates it
steps.stepSummary: רבא reinterprets רבי שמעון's second law. The second 'תנור' does not teach that the oven makes the מנחה holy. It teaches that the owner must dedicate the מנחה as an oven-baked מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Say instead that it means their dedication must be for the sake of an oven.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by changing what רבי שמעון's second law means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רבי שמעון agrees that the oven does not make the bread holy, so there is no contradiction with בית פאגי. The second mention of 'תנור' is still used, but for a different rule. When the owner sets aside the מנחה, he must say it is for an oven-baked מנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: say instead, read it this way
dedication, setting aside as holy
for the sake of, in the name of

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, רבי שמעון holds that the oven does not make a מנחה holy. The second 'תנור' only teaches that the owner must dedicate it as an oven-baked מנחה.

phrases.english: Rava said: Say,
that their consecration must be for the sake of an oven.
phrases.notes: So when the owner sets it aside, he must say it is a מנחה baked in an oven.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אֵימָא, שֶׁיְּהֵא הֶקְדֵּישָׁן לְשׁוּם תַּנּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון's second 'תנור' teaches that the oven makes the מנחה holy
steps.terutzMaskana: The second 'תנור' teaches that the owner must dedicate the מנחה for the sake of an oven-baked מנחה. The oven itself does not make it holy.

steps.title: Back to the baked מנחה: it is a voluntary offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה about a מנחת מאפה. A ברייתא learns from 'וכי תקריב' that the oven-baked מנחה is a voluntary offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If someone says: It is on me to bring a baked מנחה, he may not bring half...' The Rabbis taught: 'And when you bring' means whenever you choose to bring it, as a voluntary matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section by quoting the משנה from step 14 again. It begins a ברייתא on the פסוק, and this sets up רבי יהודה's source in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'וכי תקריב' sound like 'if you decide to bring.' So this מנחה is not a required offering. It is a free-will offering that a person takes on himself, for example with a vow.

keyTerms.meaning: a meal offering baked in an oven
half
a voluntary matter, not an obligation

phrases.english: It is upon me to bring a baked meal offering,
he may not bring half [etc.].
The Rabbis taught: 'And when you bring' –
when you bring,
to make it a voluntary matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי עָלַי מִנְחַת מַאֲפֵה, לֹא יָבִיא מֶחֱצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the oven discussion and returns to the second ruling of the משנה (step 14)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The oven-baked מנחה is a voluntary offering, learned from 'וכי תקריב'

steps.title: רבי יהודה: one offering, not a mix of חלות and רקיקין
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns from the words 'קרבן מנחה' that a person who vows a מנחת מאפה may not bring half חלות and half רקיקין. The פסוק speaks of one offering, not two or three.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A meal offering': רבי יהודה said: Where do we learn that someone who says 'It is on me to bring a baked מנחה' may not bring half loaves and half wafers? The פסוק says 'a meal offering.' I told you one offering, not two or three offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a פסוק as the source for the משנה's rule that you cannot mix חלות and רקיקין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'קרבן מנחה' is singular, so it means one offering. If someone brought half חלות and half רקיקין, it would be like two different offerings. This supports the תנא קמא of the משנה against רבי שמעון, who allowed mixing because it is one קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: thick loaves
thin wafers
the פסוק teaches
one offering

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא's rule against mixing חלות and רקיקין comes from 'קרבן מנחה': the פסוק wants one kind of offering. רבי שמעון disagrees and treats the mix as one קרבן.
steps.whyThisMatters: Both sides use the idea of 'one קרבן.' רבי יהודה says mixing turns it into two offerings. רבי שמעון says it is still one offering.

phrases.english: 'A meal offering' –
Rabbi Yehuda said: From where do we know
regarding one who says 'It is upon me to bring a baked meal offering,'
that he may not bring half loaves
and half wafers?
The verse states 'a meal offering' –
I told you one offering,
phrases.notes: He means all the breads must be the same kind.

phrases.english: and not two or three offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן לְאוֹמֵר הֲרֵי עָלַי מִנְחַת מַאֲפֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא to give the source for the משנה's ruling
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's ruling (תנא קמא) that one may not bring half חלות and half רקיקין
steps.raayaSupportSource: The singular phrase 'קרבן מנחה' in ויקרא 2:4, read as 'one offering'

steps.title: רבי שמעון begins his reply to רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא introduces רבי שמעון's response to רבי יהודה's proof from 'קרבן מנחה'. The content of his reply continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said to him (to רבי יהודה):
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. The ברייתא tells us that רבי שמעון is about to answer רבי יהודה, and his actual words continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה just argued that the words 'קרבן מנחה' mean one single offering, so you cannot mix חלות and רקיקין. The phrase 'אמר לו' shows that רבי שמעון is turning directly to רבי יהודה to push back on that proof. His argument continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי יהודה, who just gave his proof from 'קרבן מנחה' in the ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens רבי שמעון's response to רבי יהודה's proof in Step 21. The words of the response continue on the next amud.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Aimed at רבי יהודה's proof from 'קרבן מנחה' that חלות and רקיקין cannot be mixed. The full content continues on the next amud.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not yet stated. This line only introduces רבי שמעון's reply.
